If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to counteract downward bias.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative over 2 consecutive days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% starting from day 15 onward.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows upward trend, reduce slope by 0.5–1.0% per day in mid-horizon (days 11–20) to prevent momentum overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is trending downward, reverse the last 3 forecast points by +0.5–1.0% to align with sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is trending upward, reduce the last 3 forecast points by +0.5–1.0% to reflect sentiment drag.
